newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Libya challenges U.S. on human rights record.
newsitem.headline: Libya challenges U.S. on human rights record.

text.p: Libya rejected on Thursday U.S. accusations of human rights abuses against its citizens and challenged Washington to stage a comparitive examination of how the two countries treated their people.
The U.S. State Department last week in its annual rights report described the Libyan government as a "repressive regime" responsible for the systematic denial of human rights.

"The Great Jamahiriya (Libya) is ready to enter into a competitive examination with the United States in the human rights field," Libya's foreign affairs ministry said in a statement carried by the official Libyan news agency JANA.

"Libya cares about man's dignity and believes in his right to self-determination...while in the United States he is controlled by terrorist and repressive organs such as the Central Intelligence Agency and the Federal Bureau of Investigation," it said.
"We are certain that we will win such a competition and we cannot accept that the State Department can outbid us in the human rights field," the agency, monitored in Tunis, added.
